Although the game may seem short, it will still be one of the best times you will have in your life.

Might be the best puzzle game... ever made. Absolutely the gold standard for the puzzle/platform genre. The ingenuity of the puzzles and situations are mind-boggling: original, logically consistent and exceedingly clever. The pacing is superb. And that's just in the game play department. The writing, especially for dialogue, is sheer genius. The voice performances are out of this world. The graphics, while no longer gorgeous, are still more than serviceable nearly ten years on.

The above only takes into consideration the single-player campaign. There's an entire campaign available for co-operative play, as well. That's something of a rarity in the modern-ish era. Since co-op play is still a game mode desired by many gamers, it's inclusion in "Portal 2" is just one more reason this game is rightfully considered one of the best.

10/10, all the thumbs up. Recommended for: everyone that played the first "Portal"; fans of puzzles; fans of platformers; devotees of Valve's catalog; those who enjoy humor in their games; people wanting games that seamlessly merge game play and storytelling.

The sequel to my favorite game. When I was 8 and we still had the family Xbox, I begged my parents to buy this game for me. One day they did, and I played it more times than I could count or possibly remember. This is still a very special game to me today, and I consider it an essential experience along with its predecessor.

You know a game is great when it manages to not only entertain you with subtle humor and sweet action, but also impress you every so often and, what's more, stimulate your creativity and imagination. In this regard, Portal 2 is /definitely/ a great game, and worth your every dollar (or, well, whichever currency you're willing to spend).

Portal 2 is the sequal to one of the most amazing 3D puzzle platformers of all time. Your portal gun is the same, but you're methods have expanded immensly. Use Lazers, spring-loaded plates, new cubes, and so many more tools! New characters include the voice of Apperture's President, Cave Johnson and The charmingly morronic Wheatly (Voiced by the hilarious Stephen Merchant). These are but a few examples. For an even greater challenge (and a completely independant story line from single player), grab a buddy and play the Multiplayer game with two adorable robots put through tests even Chell(main character from single player) would never have been put through! I recomend this game just as highly as I would the first installment. If you liked Portal, you will love Portal 2.
